title: Cap. II Arg. 7: Apoc. 3:11 — hold fast / crown grounds foresight-perseverance
pass_a_gloss: The last testimony is taken from Revelation 3:11: Hold what you have, lest another take your crown. From these words it is plain that the crown of glory can be lost by an impious life: God therefore predestines no one to this crown of glory except because he sees that that person will persevere to the end in piety and faith. For if he predestined anyone without this foresight, predestination would be rendered uncertain, and the one whom God willed to predestine to glory could fall from glory through his own weakness or wickedness.
pass_b_english: Last: they take Revelation 3:11 — "Hold what you have, lest another take your crown." From that they say the crown of glory can be lost by an ungodly life, so God predestines no one to that crown unless he sees the person will persevere to the end in piety and faith. Without that foresight, they argue, predestination would be unsure — someone God meant for glory could drop out by weakness or wickedness.
source_text: Ultimum testimonium petitur ex Apoc. iii. 11. Tene quod habes, ne alius accipiat coronam tuam. Ex hisce verbis patet coronam gloriae amitti posse vita impia: Deus ergo neminem praedestinat ad hanc coronam gloriae, nisi quia videt illum ad extremum in pietate & fide perseveraturum. Si enim absque hac praevisione quenquam praedestinaret, incerta redderetur praedestinatio, & posset per suam infirmitatem aut pravitatem a gloria excidere, quem Deus voluit ad gloriam praedestinare.
